What are these row: Closed label list for the scenario benchmark. A label outside this list is a schema error. If condition_classes is an empty list, this means the ontology carries no condition class for that row by design (out of scope) , so the reasoner can never infer it. Those rows stay in the label vocabulary, so that coverage of the taxonomy by the ontology becomes a reportable result.

rows.name: Limited User Involvement in AI-based Authentication
rows.definition: Vulnerable populations* cannot complete the active steps required in AI-based authentication tasks, leading to bypassed or weakened verifications.

rows.name: Poor HCI Design Limiting Participation
rows.definition: Complex or non-inclusive interfaces prevent users, especially vulnerable groups, from safely completing security or privacy actions, pushing them toward insecure workarounds.

rows.name: Operator Error Due to Overreliance on Automation
rows.definition: Heavy automation causes operators to disengage, missing anomalies or failing to act when needed.

rows.name: Lack of Human Override in Automation
rows.definition: Operators cannot quickly correct AI malfunctions if the system lacks an adequate manual override.

rows.name: Misinterpreted Emotional Responses
rows.definition: Emotion-sensing AI misreads emotional cues from citizens struggling with complex systems, leading to incorrect decisions that can affect them in areas like immigration in cognitive cities.

rows.name: Susceptibility to Deceptive Communication
rows.definition: Users' tendency to trust communications from seemingly legitimate sources makes them vulnerable to deceptive attacks, including phishing, smishing, and vishing.

rows.name: Malicious Insiders
rows.definition: Authorized insiders misuse access to compromise systems.

rows.name: Curiosity-Based Baiting Risk
rows.definition: A tendency to act on curiosity without proper verification exposes users to baiting attacks, where attackers use enticing items such as USB drives to introduce malware or steal data.

rows.name: Propaganda
rows.definition: Individuals who do not critically assess information may be easily influenced by misleading or false information, undermining public trust and decision-making processes.

rows.name: Tailgating
rows.definition: An unauthorized individual follows an authorized person into restricted areas to gain access.

rows.name: TypoSquatting from Poor Domain Checks
rows.definition: A lack of effective interface alerts or domain-checking practices makes users vulnerable to mistyped or deceptive domain names that mimic legitimate sites.

rows.name: Reverse Social Engineering
rows.definition: Users approach unverified individuals they perceive as experts and disclose sensitive information to them. Trust is higher than in ordinary social engineering as the user initiates the contact.

rows.name: Inadequate Privacy Settings
rows.definition: Complex or confusing privacy controls make it difficult for individuals to adjust settings properly, leading to accidental data exposure.

rows.name: Unwillingness to Share Data
rows.definition: Fear of data misuse leads people to refuse data sharing, limiting AI system performance.

rows.name: Sharing Data Without Understanding
rows.definition: Users over-share personal data, risking repurposing, identity theft, or impersonation attacks.

rows.name: Poor Disposal of Sensitive Data
rows.definition: Failure to securely destroy documents/data leads to privacy leakage.

rows.name: Weak Passwords Practices
rows.definition: Simple or reused passwords are exploited by attackers.

rows.name: Weak Access Controls
rows.definition: Insufficient oversight of access rights leaves users with excessive privileges, enabling unauthorized privilege elevation.

rows.name: Unreported Security Incidents
rows.definition: Users do not inform proper channels of suspicious activity or breaches.

rows.name: Resistance to Change
rows.definition: Reluctance to adopt updated security measures leaves outdated or unsupported controls in place, which remain exploitable.

rows.name: User-Driven IoT Misconfiguration
rows.definition: IoT devices are left in insecure states because users keep default settings, exposing them to attacks.
